key_insight: lPINN moves most of PINN training offline by learning a frozen nonlinear basis, then solves each new differential-equation instance with only a fast online linear fit under physics constraints.
engineering_relevance: This makes physics-informed solving much faster and more scalable for forward and inverse PDE problems, especially when data or residual measurements are limited.
method: Pretrain continuous neural basis functions on an ensemble of solution data using derivatives or physics residuals.
Freeze the hidden layers and solve new instances by optimizing the governing-equation residual plus boundary, initial, regularization, and observation terms.
Use automatic differentiation so the learned basis remains differentiable and transferable across mesh resolutions.
evidence_signal: The paper reports forward and inverse tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution/parameter errors and about 10x to over 1000x faster online inference than vanilla PINNs.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the offline training ensemble, and the method may be less robust if the pretrained basis does not span the target solution family.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
